question: What is our overall settlement fail rate?

runs.headline: Settlement fail rate stands at 3.8 percent
runs.narrative: Harborline Global Custody is failing to settle 3.8% of all instructions across its matched settled and failed population. This rate represents a material operational risk that impacts client confidence and regulatory standing. Immediate root-cause analysis and remediation of systemic failure points should be prioritized.
runs.sql:
SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE settlement_status = 'FAILED') / COUNT(*), 2) AS fail_rate_pct FROM harborline.stl_trade_instruction WHERE settlement_status IN ('SETTLED', 'FAILED')
LIMIT 1000

question: Which counterparties' settlement fails cost us the most in penalties?

runs.headline: Top 4 counterparties drive $611.9K in settlement penalties
runs.narrative: Hawick Dunn Securities ($211.2K), Kendal Prowse Securities ($204.8K), Ilkley Marr Trust ($107.1K), and Nantwich Strand Bank ($88.9K) account for 60% of the $1.02M total penalty exposure across 60 counterparties. All four are tier D, reflecting elevated fail risk. Hawick Dunn's penalties are operational, tied to instruction re-establishment post-migration, while Kendal Prowse remains chronic after a failed 90-day remediation plan; further deterioration would trigger a client routing recommendation (INC-2026-019 §3, INC-2026-012 §3). Concentration in a small group of low-reliability counterparties signals need to accelerate remediation or escalate client notifications.
runs.sql: SELECT cp.counterparty_name, cp.reliability_tier, ROUND(SUM(p.penalty_amount_usd), 2) AS total_penalties_usd FROM harborline.stl_fail_penalty p JOIN harborline.dim_counterparty cp ON cp.counterparty_key = p.counterparty_key GROUP BY cp.counterparty_name, cp.reliability_tier ORDER BY total_penalties_usd DESC LIMIT 100

runs.headline: Top 2 counterparties drive $416M in settlement penalties
runs.narrative: Hawick Dunn Securities and Kendal Prowse Securities together account for $416.0K in penalties across all periods. Hawick Dunn's fails stem from operational instruction gaps post-migration, while Kendal Prowse's chronic inventory shortfalls have persisted despite a 90-day remediation plan (INC-2026-012 §3). Both are tier D counterparties; penalties on counterparty-attributed fails are claimed through the CSD monthly settlement process (POL-002 §5), but Kendal Prowse's lack of improvement raises escalation risk—a second failed review would trigger recommendation to clients to route trades elsewhere (INC-2026-012 §3).
runs.sql: SELECT cp.counterparty_name, cp.reliability_tier, ROUND(SUM(p.penalty_amount_usd), 2) AS total_penalties_usd FROM harborline.stl_fail_penalty p JOIN harborline.dim_counterparty cp ON cp.counterparty_key = p.counterparty_key GROUP BY cp.counterparty_name, cp.reliability_tier ORDER BY total_penalties_usd DESC LIMIT 100

question: Which Platinum clients missed their SLA settlement target last month?

runs.headline: Eight Platinum clients fell short of 99% settlement target
runs.narrative: All eight Platinum clients missed the required 99.0% on-time settlement rate (POL-001 §2) in September 2026, with rates ranging from 93.4% to 98.3%. Eastgate Capital Partners was furthest off at 93.42%, representing 267 unsettled instructions against its 4,136 total. Each client is entitled to a 5% custody fee credit per breached commitment, capped at 20% monthly (POL-001 §3), unless the failures stem from counterparty action or market outages (POL-003).
runs.sql:
SELECT c.client_name, c.sla_tier, d.year_num, d.month_num, COUNT(*) AS instructions, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE i.actual_settle_date_key = i.intended_settle_date_key) / COUNT(*), 2) AS settlement_rate_pct, 99.0 AS target_pct, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE i.actual_settle_date_key = i.intended_settle_date_key) / COUNT(*), 2) >= 99.0 AS met_target FROM harborline.stl_trade_instruction i JOIN harborline.dim_client c ON c.client_key = i.client_key JOIN harborline.dim_date d ON d.date_key = i.intended_settle_date_key WHERE i.settlement_status IN ('SETTLED', 'FAILED') AND c.sla_tier = 'PLATINUM' AND d.year_num = 2026 AND d.month_num = 9 GROUP BY c.client_name, c.sla_tier, d.year_num, d.month_num HAVING ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE i.actual_settle_date_key = i.intended_settle_date_key) / COUNT(*), 2) < 99.0 ORDER BY settlement_rate_pct
LIMIT 1000

runs.headline: Eight Platinum clients fell below 99.0% settlement rate in September
runs.narrative: All eight Platinum clients missed their 99.0% settlement target (POL-001 §2) in September 2026, with rates ranging from 93.4% to 98.3%. Eastgate Capital Partners posted the largest shortfall at 93.4% across 4,136 instructions, while the remaining seven clients clustered between 96.8% and 98.3%. Each breach entitles the affected client to SLA credits of 5.0% of that month's custody fee, capped at 20.0% monthly (POL-001 §3).
runs.sql:
SELECT c.client_name, c.sla_tier, d.year_num, d.month_num, COUNT(*) AS instructions, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE i.actual_settle_date_key = i.intended_settle_date_key) / COUNT(*), 2) AS settlement_rate_pct, 99.0 AS target_pct, 100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE i.actual_settle_date_key = i.intended_settle_date_key) / COUNT(*) >= 99.0 AS met_target FROM harborline.stl_trade_instruction i JOIN harborline.dim_client c ON c.client_key = i.client_key JOIN harborline.dim_date d ON d.date_key = i.intended_settle_date_key WHERE i.settlement_status IN ('SETTLED', 'FAILED') AND c.sla_tier = 'PLATINUM' AND d.year_num = 2026 AND d.month_num = 9 GROUP BY c.client_name, c.sla_tier, d.year_num, d.month_num HAVING 100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE i.actual_settle_date_key = i.intended_settle_date_key) / COUNT(*) < 99.0 ORDER BY settlement_rate_pct ASC
LIMIT 1000

runs.narrative: All eight Platinum clients examined failed to meet the 99.0% on-time settlement rate (POL-001 §2) in September 2026, with compliance ranging from 93.4% to 98.3%. Eastgate Capital Partners, handling the largest volume at 4,136 instructions, showed the steepest shortfall at 93.4%, while Westmark and Montclair each achieved 98.3%—closest to target but still 66 basis points short. Each client is eligible for a 5% custody fee credit per breached commitment, capped at 20% monthly (POL-001 §3), unless the failures resulted from counterparty issues or market infrastructure outages.

question: Which corporate action elections did we miss, and what was the notice window?

runs.headline: 44 missed corporate action elections, all with 1-day notice
runs.narrative: All 44 missed elections had a notice window of just 1 business day—the minimum threshold under our client deadline policy (POL-004 §4), which sets the internal deadline one business day ahead of the market deadline. With such compressed timeframes, even routine processing delays resulted in missed deadlines; the largest single exposure was $3.9M on a tender offer announced 2025-09-04. These events likely qualify as short-notice under POL-004 §5, requiring same-day notification and direct manager contact for PLATINUM and GOLD clients—processes that may have been insufficient to ensure timely client instruction submission.
runs.sql: WITH missed AS (SELECT event_key, client_key, election_key, estimated_client_impact_usd FROM harborline.cae_client_election WHERE missed_deadline) SELECT e.event_ref, e.event_type, e.notice_window_days, m.client_key, m.election_key, m.estimated_client_impact_usd, dd.full_date AS announcement_date FROM missed m JOIN harborline.cae_event e ON e.event_key=m.event_key JOIN harborline.dim_date dd ON dd.date_key=e.announcement_date_key ORDER BY e.notice_window_days ASC, m.estimated_client_impact_usd DESC LIMIT 100

runs.headline: 44 missed elections with 1-day notice window
runs.narrative: Harborline missed 44 corporate action elections across all periods in the data, each with only 1 business day between announcement and the client response deadline. All 44 events fell into the short-notice category (POL-004 §5), where issuer deadlines left minimal time for client instruction and Harborline's required one-day processing buffer (POL-004 §4). The largest single exposure was a $3.9M tender offer (client 45, election 2160); cumulative estimated impact across the top 8 visible events alone exceeds $22.3M, with 36 additional missed elections in the dataset.
runs.sql: WITH missed AS (SELECT event_key, client_key, election_key, estimated_client_impact_usd FROM harborline.cae_client_election WHERE missed_deadline) SELECT e.event_ref, e.event_type, e.notice_window_days, m.client_key, m.election_key, m.estimated_client_impact_usd FROM missed m JOIN harborline.cae_event e ON e.event_key=m.event_key ORDER BY e.notice_window_days ASC, m.estimated_client_impact_usd DESC LIMIT 100

runs.headline: 44 missed corporate action elections, all with 1-day notice
runs.narrative: We failed to act on 44 corporate action elections across all periods in the data, each with only a 1-day notice window. The four largest misses—two tender offers and two mergers or dividend options—carried combined client impact of $14.5M. A 1-day notice window leaves minimal margin for decision and execution; systemic process gaps or calendar misalignment likely drove the uniform notice constraint across all events.
runs.sql: WITH missed AS (SELECT event_key, client_key, election_key, estimated_client_impact_usd FROM harborline.cae_client_election WHERE missed_deadline) SELECT e.event_ref, e.event_type, e.notice_window_days, m.client_key, m.election_key, m.estimated_client_impact_usd FROM missed m JOIN harborline.cae_event e ON e.event_key=m.event_key ORDER BY e.notice_window_days ASC, m.estimated_client_impact_usd DESC LIMIT 100

question: Which counterparties meet our tier-D criteria?

runs.headline: Seven counterparties in tier D exceed 10% fail rate
runs.narrative: All seven counterparties—Jedburgh Colt, Lyndhurst Boyd, Ilkley Marr, Nantwich Strand, Hawick Dunn, Kendal Prowse, and Malvern Ley—meet tier D criteria (fail rate above 10.0% and average days failed above 4.0 days) over the trailing 12 months (POL-007 §2). Fail rates range from 12.3% to 13.6%, with each counterparty averaging 6.5–7.4 days per failed instruction. Tier D status triggers mandatory pre-matching, daily fail reporting, client notification, and a 90-day remediation plan; Kendal Prowse and Hawick Dunn remain in tier D despite prior review cycles and incident responses (INC-2026-012 §3, INC-2026-019 §1), and continued non-improvement may lead Harborline to recommend clients route trades elsewhere (POL-007 §4).
runs.sql:
WITH latest AS (SELECT MAX(d.full_date) AS max_date FROM harborline.stl_trade_instruction i JOIN harborline.dim_date d ON d.date_key = i.intended_settle_date_key), perf AS (SELECT cp.counterparty_name, cp.reliability_tier AS assigned_tier, COUNT(*) AS instructions, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE i.settlement_status = 'FAILED') AS failed_instructions, ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE i.settlement_status = 'FAILED') / COUNT(*), 2) AS fail_rate_pct, ROUND(AVG(i.days_failed) FILTER (WHERE i.settlement_status = 'FAILED'), 2) AS avg_days_failed FROM harborline.stl_trade_instruction i JOIN harborline.dim_counterparty cp ON cp.counterparty_key = i.counterparty_key JOIN harborline.dim_date d ON d.date_key = i.intended_settle_date_key CROSS JOIN latest l WHERE i.settlement_status IN ('SETTLED', 'FAILED') AND d.full_date > l.max_date - INTERVAL 12 MONTH AND (i.fail_reason_code IS NULL OR i.fail_reason_code <> 'MARKET_RESTRICTION') GROUP BY cp.counterparty_name, cp.reliability_tier) SELECT counterparty_name, assigned_tier, instructions, failed_instructions, fail_rate_pct, avg_days_failed FROM perf WHERE fail_rate_pct > 10 AND avg_days_failed > 4 ORDER BY fail_rate_pct DESC
LIMIT 1000

Jedburgh Colt Securities leads with a 13.6% fail rate and Kendal Prowse has the highest instruction volume at 9,375, yet remains in tier D after a July 2026 remediation review showed no improvement (INC-2026-012 §3).
